title: The gate records what each governed write leaves, and a commit-msg hook compares it with the commit

context.task: The record in git (ADR-016, ROADMAP V3). The write gate records, before it allows a governed Edit, MultiEdit or Write, the content the file has and the content the write leaves, with the receipts that cover it, and denies the write when it cannot record them. A new git hook, tools/git/commit-msg, appends to every commit message, for each governed path whose content the commit changes, a trailer that says whether recorded writes lead from the content at HEAD to the committed content, with the rationales of their receipts. It only records; it never refuses a commit. The installer installs it next to the pre-commit. AGENTS.md states it and declares its limits. The installer's questions, its no-questions mode, pip and the commit are the next contract's.

select.heading: ADR-016 — El acta en git (2026-10-14, autor)

problem: The audit trail records that a write was asked for and approved, not that it happened, and it lives in a local database that git ignores. The README promises that every action leaves a record that it happened, and why. ADR-016 decided how to make that true: the gate, which already runs before every governed write, computes what the write leaves and records it, denying the write when it cannot; a commit-msg hook compares the committed content of each governed path with what the recorded writes left and writes the result, with the rationales of their receipts, as trailers of the commit message. The hook only records: it never refuses a commit. Today the gate opens the database only to read, nothing compares a commit with the receipts, and the installer installs only the pre-commit hook.
decisions: D1 Order of the edits. A hook is read again on every call, also by the session that implements this contract, and a gate that raises denies every governed write, including the one that would repair it. So: (a) tools/boundary_validator/hook_gate.py gains WRITES_DDL, receipt_case, record_write and recorded_writes (D2-D5), with their tests passing in process, while the hook still calls has_receipt; (b) then one edit makes tools/hooks/require_boundary_validation.py compute and record (D6), its tests written first and seen red; (c) tools/git/commit_record.py, then tools/git/commit-msg; (d) tools/install.py; (e) AGENTS.md. Each edit leaves every hook working.

D2 The table, owned by hook_gate (the module that owns the location of the audit trail; the validator does not change): WRITES_DDL = CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS writes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, timestamp TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')), target_file TEXT NOT NULL, tool TEXT NOT NULL, before_sha256 TEXT, after_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, receipts TEXT NOT NULL). target_file is the repository-relative POSIX path of the target as the gate spells it after canonical() (the stored spelling); before_sha256 is NULL when the file did not exist; receipts is a JSON array of case_ids.

D3 receipt_case(file_path, block_sha256, grounding_sha256=None, window_seconds=project_config.DEFAULT_WINDOW) -> str | None: the case_id of the most recent receipt (latest timestamp, then highest rowid) within the window that names file_path (as _names resolves it) and has that block_sha256 and, unless grounding_sha256 is None, that grounding_sha256; None when there is none. It opens the database read-only, as _recent_receipts does, and raises on what it cannot read. has_receipt and has_any_receipt keep their behaviour.

D4 record_write(target_file, tool, before_sha256, after_sha256, receipts) -> None: opens the database at _db_path() with the URI mode=rw, so that it never creates a database file nor its directory; in one transaction executes WRITES_DDL and inserts the row, receipts stored as json.dumps of the list; closes the connection. Any sqlite3.Error or OSError propagates.

D5 recorded_writes(target_file) -> list of (before_sha256 or None, after_sha256, rationales), in id order, for the rows whose target_file equals target_file exactly. rationales is, in the order of the row's case_ids with each case_id taken once, the rationale that audit_log holds for that case_id, or None when audit_log has no such row or its rationale is NULL. Read-only (mode=ro). A database without a writes table gives []. A missing database, a database without audit_log, or any other error raises.

D6 What the hook does. For Edit, MultiEdit and Write on a governed path, the decision uses receipt_case for each receipt the tool needs (required_receipts), in place of has_receipt: the write passes the receipt check when every one returns a case_id. After that check and the primitive check pass: the hook reads the file's bytes; FileNotFoundError means absent (before None); any other OSError denies, as an unverifiable write. before_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the bytes. The result is the content for a Write, and for an Edit or a MultiEdit written_result over the bytes decoded as strict UTF-8; when they are not UTF-8 (a governed .py file is denied as today by the primitive check) or written_result is None, nothing is recorded and the write is allowed, as today. Otherwise the hook calls record_write(target relative to REPO_ROOT as POSIX, tool, before_sha256, SHA-256 of result.encode('utf-8'), the case_ids in the order of required_receipts). When record_write raises, the hook exits 2 with one line on stderr that starts with "[require_boundary_validation] ", names the target, the rule and its source, says that the gate could not record in the audit trail what the write leaves and so denies it, and gives the error. The file is read once for the primitive check and the record. NotebookEdit and the tools the gate does not know record nothing, and their decisions do not change; a denied write records nothing. The docstrings of the hook and of hook_gate say what the gate now writes; its receipt queries stay read-only.

D7 tools/git/commit-msg, a POSIX sh script with the mode of tools/git/pre-commit in the tree: it runs python3 "$top/tools/git/commit_record.py" "$1", where top is git rev-parse --show-toplevel. When either fails it writes on stderr one line starting with "[commit_record] " that says the record was not made, with the exit status, and that the commit goes on. It always exits 0.

D8 tools/git/commit_record.py starts as tools/git/commit_integrity.py does: the lines that put the repository root on sys.path only to import tools, then a try that imports tools.project_config, tools.audit.run_process and tools.boundary_validator.hook_gate and, on any exception, writes "[commit_record] cannot start (<type>: <message>)" on stderr and exits 1. Standard library otherwise, postponed annotations, importable under Python 3.9. Every git command goes through run_process and inherits the environment, so GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_DIR are honoured. It takes one argument, the path of the message file; any other usage exits 2 with a usage line on stderr.

D9 Which paths. The repository is git rev-parse --show-toplevel. The base is HEAD, or the empty tree before the first commit, found as commit_integrity._base finds it. The entries are those of git diff-index --cached --raw --no-renames --no-abbrev -z --ignore-submodules=none <base>, in git's order, each with its old and new side (mode and blob, or absent when the mode is 000000). An entry gets a record when project_config.governance(path) governs it, neither side is a gitlink (mode 160000), and its content changes: the blob ids differ, which includes an addition and a deletion; a change of mode alone gets no record. The content of a side is the SHA-256 of the bytes git cat-file blob <oid> prints; an absent side is None. tools.audit.run_process gives that output as UTF-8 text, which encodes back to the same bytes; a blob that is not valid UTF-8 gets a value that matches no recorded write (the gate records only UTF-8 results), so as the committed side it reads as changed outside the channel and as the base side no recorded write starts from it.

D10 The chain. With start the content at the base and end the committed content: end None (a deletion) is changed outside the channel. Otherwise, when hook_gate.audit_trail_exists() is false there are no recorded writes; when it is true the writes are recorded_writes(path). reached maps a content to the list of writes that lead to it from start, beginning as {start: []}; for each write in id order, when its before is in reached and its after is not, reached[after] = reached[before] + [write] (None before and None start both mean absent). The path matches when end is in reached; its writes are reached[end]. No time bound applies: a write recorded at any time can be part of the chain.

D11 The lines, one trailer each, in the order of the entries. A path that matches: "Actuarii-Record: matches: <path>", followed by one "Actuarii-Rationale: <text>" per distinct rationale of its chain's writes, in the order they first appear; a rationale's runs of whitespace (line breaks included) become one space and it is stripped; None becomes "(none recorded)". Any other path: "Actuarii-Record: changed outside the channel: <path>". A path that holds a control character (U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F) is written as json.dumps of it; any other path as it is. When no entry gets a record, the script changes nothing: the message stays byte for byte.

D12 It never refuses a commit. Any error while the lines are computed (an invalid project configuration, a git command that fails, an audit database that cannot be read, an OSError) replaces all the lines with one "Actuarii-Record: not made: <reason>", the reason on one line with runs of whitespace as one space, and the script goes on to D13 and exits 0. A missing audit database is not an error: it means no recorded writes.

D13 Writing the message. When the message, cut before the first line that ends with " ------------------------ >8 ------------------------" and without the lines git stripspace --strip-comments removes, holds only whitespace, the script changes nothing and exits 0: git then aborts the commit as empty, and a trailer must not turn that into a commit. Otherwise it runs git interpret-trailers --in-place --where end --if-exists add --if-missing add --no-divider, with one --trailer per line in order, on the message file. When that fails, or the message cannot be read, it writes one line starting with "[commit_record] " on stderr and exits 1; tools/git/commit-msg then lets the commit go on. The script writes the message file in no other way.

D14 The installer installs tools/git/commit-msg where git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg says, with exactly the rules, conflicts, skip and mode 0755 of the pre-commit hook (only inside the target's own .git), the pre-commit first and then the commit-msg in the plan and the report. Its docstring says so. Nothing else of the installer changes.

D15 AGENTS.md. The title line becomes "# AGENTS.md — Agent constitution (v2.3.0)". After 2.6, a new clause, word for word: "2.7 A commit carries the record of its governed paths. **[enforced]** Before it allows an `Edit`, `MultiEdit` or `Write` on a governed path, the write gate records in the audit trail the content the file has and the content the write leaves, computed from the tool's input, with the receipts that cover it, and denies the write when it cannot record them. The git hook `tools/git/commit-msg`, which the person installs as `.git/hooks/commit-msg`, appends to the message of every commit, for each governed path whose content the commit changes, an `Actuarii-Record` trailer: `matches` when recorded writes lead from the content at `HEAD` to the committed content, followed by one `Actuarii-Rationale` trailer per distinct `Rationale` of their receipts, and `changed outside the channel` otherwise. It only records: it never refuses a commit, and when it cannot make the record it says so (`not made`)." In section 9, the bullet "Commits around the hook" becomes, word for word: "* **Commits around the hooks.** `git commit --no-verify` and git's internal commands (`commit-tree`, `update-ref`) skip both hooks, and `git merge` does not run the pre-commit; the person approves each of those commands. The hooks work only where the person installed them (the session announcement says whether the pre-commit is), and with `core.fileMode` off the pre-commit's mode check can refuse a valid commit." After the bullet "What leaves a record", two new bullets, word for word: "* **What the commit record compares.** The gate computes what `Edit`, `MultiEdit` and `Write` leave from their input, as UTF-8 text; it records nothing for `NotebookEdit`, for a tool it does not know, or for an `Edit` it cannot apply to the file as it reads it (a file that is not UTF-8, an `old_string` it does not find). Where Claude Code writes something other than its input says (other line endings, other quotes, another encoding), or git stores something other than the file (a clean filter), the record says `changed outside the channel` for a file that went through the gate: it says `matches` only when recorded writes reach the committed content. A committed file that is not UTF-8 text always reads as changed outside the channel. A write the gate allowed and that never happened counts when the same content reaches the commit another way. Modes are not compared, and a submodule gets no record." and "* **Where the commit record is made.** Only where git runs `commit-msg`: `git commit` and `git merge`, without `--no-verify`, in a repository where the hook is installed. A rebase or a cherry-pick copies the trailers of a commit without checking them again, and an amended commit is compared with the commit it replaces. Writes recorded in another clone are not in this audit trail, so what they left reads as changed outside the channel. The trailers are text in a message: anyone can write them, and nothing signs them." Nothing else of AGENTS.md changes.

D16 Tests. Tests of the gate run in process as tests/security/test_content_receipt.py does (the real validator for receipts, the real hook on a replaced stdin, the database the conftest isolates); a governed file that must exist lives under tmp_path, with the REPO_ROOT attributes of the hook, hook_gate and the validator pointed there, never in the repository. Tests of the commit record that commit for real copy the kit under tmp_path as tests/security/test_root_off_sys_path.py does, init a git repository there with HOME under tmp_path and a git identity on the command line, install the copy's tools/git/commit-msg as its .git/hooks/commit-msg, make receipts with the copy's own validator and records with the copy's own gate, run as processes, and put first on the PATH a directory whose python3 is the interpreter of the test run, so that the hook runs the copy's script and never the session's shim. No test touches the repository's own .git, .data or files. tests/security/test_hook_startup_surface.py gains commit_record.py among the modules that postpone annotations and a test of its import surface; tests/security/test_root_off_sys_path.py gains it among SCRIPTS and HANDLERS (its startup failure: exit 1, "[commit_record] cannot start"). No text in tools/ or tests/ cites a clause of AGENTS.md (tests/unit/test_kit_independence.py).

D17 The validator requires a Rationale in every proposal: include it, even if the schema of validate_proposal shown to you lacks it. Once step (b) is in place, your own governed writes are recorded in the repository's audit trail; that is expected.

D18 Not in this contract: the installer's questions, its no-questions mode, pip and the commit; INSTALL.md; the session announcement of the commit-msg hook; any change to the validator, to commit_integrity.py or to the pre-commit.
D19 No new dependency and no file outside files_may_touch.

D20 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: An allowed Edit, MultiEdit or Write on a governed path whose result the gate can compute leaves one row in writes: the stored repository-relative spelling, the tool, the SHA-256 of the file before (NULL when absent), the SHA-256 of the exact result, and the case_ids of the receipts that allowed it.
When the row cannot be written, the write is denied with a message that names the target, the rule, its source and the error.

NotebookEdit, unknown tools, an Edit the gate cannot compute, a denied write and an ungoverned path record nothing, and every decision the gate made before stays the same; the gate never creates the database.

Every commit made with the hook installed carries, for each governed path whose content it changes, "Actuarii-Record: matches: <path>" with the distinct rationales of the recorded writes that lead from HEAD's content to the committed one, or "Actuarii-Record: changed outside the channel: <path>".

The hook never refuses a commit: an error becomes "Actuarii-Record: not made: <reason>", a script that cannot start is reported on stderr, a commit with no governed change keeps its message, and a message emptied to abort stays empty so that git aborts.
The installer installs the commit-msg hook as it installs the pre-commit, with the same conflicts and the same second run that writes nothing.
AGENTS.md v2.3.0 states the record in 2.7 and declares its limits in section 9.

tests.must_catch: an allowed Write, Edit or MultiEdit on a governed path that leaves no row, or a row with another path spelling (a path spelled through .. is stored canonical), tool, before hash (NULL for an absent file), after hash (the exact result) or case_ids (the most recent matching receipt, in the order of the edits)
tests.reason: at base the gate writes nothing to the audit database

tests.must_catch: a write that is allowed although its row could not be written (a writes table of another shape, a database file the gate can read but not write), or a denial that does not name the target, the rule and the error
tests.reason: at base the gate never writes, so these writes are allowed

tests.must_catch: a receipt_case that returns another case than the most recent matching one or one outside the window; a record_write that creates a missing database or its directory; a recorded_writes that fails without the writes table, loses the order, or misses a None rationale
tests.reason: at base receipt_case, record_write and recorded_writes do not exist

tests.must_catch: a row recorded for a NotebookEdit, an unknown tool, an Edit of a governed file that is not UTF-8, an Edit whose old_string is not in the file, a denied write or an ungoverned path, or a change in any of those decisions
tests.reason: at base nothing is recorded and these decisions are today's; they must stay so

tests.must_catch: a commit of a governed file written through the gate with a receipt whose message lacks "Actuarii-Record: matches: <path>" and its rationale, or a commit of a governed file changed without the gate whose message does not say "Actuarii-Record: changed outside the channel: <path>" (ROADMAP V3)
tests.reason: at base there is no commit-msg hook and no record; the test commits for real in a copy of the kit

tests.must_catch: a wrong chain or wrong lines: two gated edits not given as one matches line with their distinct rationales in order; a repeated rationale written twice; a recorded write that never happened spoiling a match; an edit by hand before or after a gated one, or a deletion, not reported as changed outside the channel; a new file written by Write not matching from absent; a line for a change of mode alone, an ungoverned path or a gitlink; a failure before the first commit; a committed governed file that is not UTF-8 not reported as changed outside the channel, or making the record fail; a rationale with a line break kept on two lines; a missing rationale not given as (none recorded); a path with a control character not written as a JSON string
tests.reason: at base tools/git/commit_record.py does not exist

tests.must_catch: a hook that refuses a commit, or loses the failure: an unreadable audit database or an invalid configuration without one not made line; a script that cannot start without its stderr line or with the commit refused; a message changed when no governed path changes; a message holding only comments, or only comments above the scissors line and a diff below it, given a trailer, or a commit made from it
tests.reason: at base there is no hook

tests.must_catch: a commit_record.py that does not postpone annotations, imports beyond the standard library, tools.project_config, tools.audit.run_process and tools.boundary_validator.hook_gate, keeps the root on sys.path, imports a module planted at the root, or ends a failed start other than in its handler
tests.reason: at base the file does not exist, so the new cases of test_hook_startup_surface.py and test_root_off_sys_path.py fail

tests.must_catch: an install that does not put the clone's commit-msg, mode 0755, where git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg says; a different or non-executable commit-msg that is not a conflict or that lets something be written; a hooks path outside the target's own .git that does not name commit-msg; a second run that writes
tests.reason: at base the installer installs only the pre-commit

tests.must_catch: a change to what holds today for the gate, the audit database, the installer, the commit check and the start-up of the hooks
tests.reason: they hold at base and must keep holding: tests/security/test_hook_gate.py, test_content_receipt.py, test_write_gate_tools.py, test_gate_primitives.py, test_missing_audit_trail.py, test_audit_database.py, test_hook_case_identity.py, test_hooks_without_shim.py, test_hook_project_dir.py, test_commit_integrity.py, test_hook_startup_surface.py::test_security_gate_never_creates_a_database, tests/unit/test_installer.py and tests/unit/test_kit_independence.py

commit_message: feat(acta): la puerta guarda lo que deja cada escritura y el commit-msg lo compara con el commit
